newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* The Federal Reserve Board's policymaking body adjourned its meeting Tuesday without changing a key short-term interest rate. Treasury prices moved higher on the decision, while stocks ended mixed.
* AT&T Corp said its third-quarter profits would be far lower than analysts' expectations, causing a steep slide in the price of its stock.
* Prudential Insurance Co of America said it would pay at least $410 million to settle long-running disputes over its sales practices.
* The Senate voted 88-10 to approve $1 billion in subsidies over the next 10 years for the nation's private merchant-marine fleet.
* A 10-million acre forestland in Ashland, Maine, and the clearcutting it has endured, is becoming a political lightning rod in this year's elections.
* International Business Machines Corp plans to unveil Wednesday its newest version of its OS/2 software, which is nicknamed Merlin.
* Sun-Diamond Growers of California was found guilty of illegally giving more than $9,000 worth of gifts to fomrer Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.
* Horizon/CMS Healthcare said Michigan's attorney general was investigating one of its nursing homes.
* A wrongful death suit against H.B. Fuller was thrown out by a federal judge in St. Paul, Minn., who said the case should be tried in Guatemala, the home of the plaintiffs.
* Pan American World Airways is offering a generous frequent-flier plan as it begins flying again with routes to Miami and Los Angeles from New York.
* An unusual lawsuit against the Glenmede Trust Co in Philadelphia could change the way investment advisers do business. - Market Place
